I am an old man now, 66 years, and this small sorghum plot behind my compound is only a little piece of land, but it feeds my household. I will buy a small bag of urea if I can manage the money at the market in Gusau, because without fertilizer the sorghum heads come out small and the Harmattan finishes them. I keep my own seed from last year's harvest like my father did — the improved seeds from the agro-dealer are too costly for such a small plot, and my local sorghum knows this soil. My sons and grandchildren will help me with the weeding and bird-scaring; I have no money to hire laborers, only maybe one or two days for a strong young man to help clear the land before the rains.
